name: Exponential Search
description: Finds the range where the target lies by doubling the index (1,2,4,8,16…), then performs binary search in that range. Especially efficient when target is near the beginning.
aim: Search by first finding a range [2^(k-1), 2^k] containing the target through exponential jumps, then applying binary search within that range.
howItWorks: Double i while arr[i] < target and i < n
Apply binary search in range [i/2, min(i, n-1)]

time.averageCase: Doubles range until target found, then binary search
time.worstCase: Same as binary search once range is found

complexity.spaceDescription: No extra space beyond index variables

realWorld: Searching very large sorted datasets where target may be near start
Used in certain string matching algorithms
whenToUse: Sorted array where target is near the beginning
When binary search would start with too large a range
alternatives: Binary Search — simpler when size is known
Jump Search — similar but fixed step size √n
Interpolation Search — better for uniform distributions
